summary: Reviewed 4da539c..fa02c30 (implementation 777641d + tests fa02c30) as a maintainer. The climberDisplay swap is correct at 12 of 16 render sites and at all 3 converted server notification sites (sender/accepter ids verified against the DB layer), the narrowed selects leave no dead code, and the /api/users/search extension preserves exact-match, self-exclusion, auth and the 60/hr fail-closed limit. One critical: the stated rule (primary = climberDisplay, secondary = @username whenever username exists) is violated at the 4 PendingChallenges rows (web + mobile) because that component has no @username sub-line at all - its secondary slot is the expiry countdown. For the default account state (ensureUser never sets display_name) a username-only challenger went from 'bobsmith challenged you' to 'Swift Ibex 42 challenged you' with no handle anywhere, and since createChallenge requires no friendship the recipient has no Friends-List row to cross-reference. The verifier's justification for not testing that component ('applies the identical two-line pattern ... + username && sub-line') is factually wrong. Four warnings: two remaining challenge notification name sites still use display_name ?? username ?? 'Your opponent'; app/tsconfig.json still lacks @app/* (verified TS2307 by compiling a touched mobile component without a paths map), which makes the 4 mobile challenge components unreachable from the root TS program and leaves the new vitest @app alias with zero consumers; isSearchable/EMAIL_SHAPE now exists in three hand-copied places; and the relaxed client gate multiplies requests against the same 60/hr budget while both search components still ignore non-ok responses. Spot-checked the two new test files (10/10 pass in 815ms); did not re-run the full suite.
goal: Maintainer review of the climberDisplay identity-resolution swap and the /api/users/search username-exact-match extension: correctness of the primary/secondary line rule at every render site, server-side id correctness, web/mobile parity, the @app alias / tsconfig gap, diff hygiene, and general readability.

findings.issue: The change's own rule (primary line = climberDisplay(id, displayName), secondary line = @username whenever username is truthy) is violated at 4 of 16 render sites. PendingChallenges / PendingChallengesSection have NO @username sub-line - the second line of those rows is timeLeft(c.expiresAt) - so swapping the name to climberDisplay strictly removes identifying information instead of relocating it. Concrete failure: (1) user B sets username 'bobsmith' in settings and never sets a display name; display_name = null is the DEFAULT for every account because ensureUser (app/src/db/user.ts:27) never writes display_name and settings can explicitly clear it. (2) B POSTs /api/challenge with recipientId = A; createChallenge (app/src/db/challenge.ts:35) has NO friendship requirement, so B can be a complete stranger. (3) A opens /duel -> Incoming challenges: climberDisplay('B', null) -> climberHandle -> 'Swift Ibex 42 challenged you', countdown underneath, and c.sender.username ('bobsmith') is present in the payload but never rendered. Pre-change that row read 'bobsmith challenged you' - a public handle A could look up at /c/bobsmith. Because there is no friendship, there is no Friends-List row (which DOES render @bobsmith) to cross-reference, so A must accept or decline with zero identifying information. Nothing prevents this: no test covers PendingChallenges, and the verifier's stated reason for skipping it - 'PendingChallenges.tsx ... apply the identical two-line pattern (climberDisplay(id, displayName) + `username &&` sub-line)' (verifier handoff feedback[3]) - is factually incorrect for this component. This is not a privacy decision: the same diff deliberately shows @username at 5 other sites, so omitting it here is an oversight.
findings.fix:
Render the handle in these 4 rows so the rule holds everywhere. Cheapest consistent option: add the same sub-line under the name inside the existing min-w-0 column, above the countdown - web PendingChallenges.tsx received block (after the `{name} challenged you`

) and sent block (after the `Waiting for {name}`

), plus the matching two blocks in mobile PendingChallengesSection.tsx: `{c.sender.username && (

@{c.sender.username}

)}` / `{c.recipient.username && ...}`. Both trees must change in the same commit (context/conventions.md). Add a render test for at least one of the two rows asserting both climberHandle(id) and '@' appear for a displayName:null sender, since no automated test touches this component today.

findings.issue: Two challenge notification name sites were not converted and still read `display_name ?? username ?? "Your opponent"`. The same person is therefore named two different ways inside one challenge flow: the challenge_received push says 'Swift Ibex 42 challenged you' (converted here) while challenge_accepted says 'bobsmith accepted your challenge' and challenge_declined says 'bobsmith declined your challenge'. The commit message claims 'the notification text in the challenge/friend API routes', and the implementer already extended scope past the 11 'Someone' sites to the 'Friend'/'User' fallbacks for exactly this consistency argument, so 'Your opponent' is the same class of placeholder left behind. Found by grepping `?? username` app-wide rather than only for "Someone", which is why neither the implementer's nor the verifier's sweep caught it.
findings.fix: accept/route.ts: `const recipientName = climberDisplay(c.recipient.id, c.recipient.display_name);` (result.challenge is ChallengeWithUsers, so recipient.id and recipient_id both exist). decline/route.ts: `const declinerName = climberDisplay(challengeBefore.recipient.id, challengeBefore.recipient.display_name);` (getChallenge returns the same include). Both notifications also put the name in `data` (recipientName), which no client reads - grep confirmed no consumers outside the routes - so there is no contract break.

findings.issue: The diff added `@app` -> src to app/vitest.config.mts (test.alias + resolve.alias) but not the matching "@app/*": ["./src/*"] to app/tsconfig.json paths, so the two toolchains now disagree about a module specifier this change introduced into production code. Verified directly, not inferred: `npx tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck --jsx react-jsx --module esnext --moduleResolution bundler mobile/src/components/challenge/FriendsListSection.tsx` reports `error TS2307: Cannot find module '@app/lib/handle'`, and there is no @app package in app/node_modules to resolve it by accident. Because tsc's `exclude` only filters the initial include glob and not the import graph, ANY root-project file that pulls one of the 4 touched mobile challenge components into the program - including a vitest test importing it by relative path - now fails `pnpm typecheck`. The verifier hit this and deleted their mobile smoke test rather than fix it, which leaves two side effects: the 4 mobile components (the tree the original bug report came from) have neither typecheck coverage (root tsconfig excludes `mobile`) nor test coverage, and the new vitest `@app` alias currently has zero consumers - `rg '@app/' app/tests` returns nothing - so it is unexercised config justified by a test that does not exist.
findings.fix: Add "@app/*": ["./src/*"] alongside "@/*" in app/tsconfig.json paths. Safe and 3 lines: no baseUrl is needed (paths resolve relative to the tsconfig, same as the existing "@/*": ["./*"]), and exclude: ["mobile", ...] keeps the default program scope unchanged - it only adds resolution. Then land one render test for a mobile challenge component so both the alias and the mobile tree are actually covered; without that test, drop the vitest alias from this diff rather than ship config with no consumer.

findings.issue: Accidental duplication of a gate that must stay in agreement across three places: `isSearchable()` is byte-identical (including its doc comment) in the web and mobile search components, and `EMAIL_SHAPE` is now declared a third time in the route, where `exactMatchFilter` re-expresses the same predicate. The comment in both components says 'Mirrors the server's gate in app/api/users/search/route.ts' - a mirror maintained by hand across three files. If the server gate ever moves (username min length, an email-shape tweak, a new accepted identifier), the clients silently drift: too strict and valid queries stop firing, too loose and every keystroke burns rate-limited requests. This change itself proves the mechanism for avoiding the copy - it is the change that started importing @app/lib/* into mobile components.
findings.fix: Export the predicate once from app/src/lib (e.g. userSearchQuery.ts exporting EMAIL_SHAPE, isSearchableQuery(q) and exactMatchFilter(q)), import it as ../../lib/userSearchQuery in the web component and @app/lib/userSearchQuery in the mobile one, and have the route call the shared exactMatchFilter. Bonus: the existing route test then covers the client gate too, and isSearchableQuery becomes one unit with three real non-test callers instead of three copies with one caller each.

findings.issue: Two interacting issues on the search path, one aggravated by this diff and one pre-existing. (a) The auto-fire gate went from 'looks like a complete email' to 'is a valid username OR a complete email', i.e. from ~3 firing prefixes near the end of an email to every prefix from 3 chars up ('cre','crea','creat','creato','creator','creator-1'). With the 300ms debounce, any pause longer than 300ms between keystrokes - routine on a phone keyboard, and the mobile Challenge screen is the primary surface - fires another request against the same unchanged 60/hr failMode:'closed' budget, so a user now gets materially fewer completed searches per hour before lockout. (b) Pre-existing but now much more likely to be reached: both components do `if (res.ok) { ... }` with no else branch, so a 429 (or any non-2xx) produces no error message, leaves `searched` false so even the 'No user found' line stays hidden, and does NOT clear `results`. The rendered outcome is a stale result row for the PREVIOUS query still showing its Add/Challenge button while the input shows a different handle - one click adds the wrong person. The design-review checklist requires an error state for every changed component; this one has loading and empty but no error.
findings.fix: Add the missing failure branch in both components: on !res.ok clear results and set a user-visible message (distinguish 429 -> 'Too many searches, try again in a while'), and clear results in the catch as well. Consider only auto-firing at a longer prefix (or on Enter/blur) for the username branch so a mobile typist cannot spend 6 of 60 requests on one lookup. Not strictly introduced here, but (a) is.

findings.issue: `const showUsername = friend.user.username !== null;` is the only one of the 6 sub-line gates that uses an explicit null compare; the other five (FriendRequests x2, UserSearch, FriendsListSection, UserSearchSection) use truthy `username &&`. Functionally identical today because normalizeUsername enforces a 3-char minimum, but `!== null` renders '@undefined' if the key is ever absent from the JSON rather than null, and the point of this diff is one uniform rule. Correction for the record: the verifier's info finding states FriendsListSection.tsx also uses `!== null`; it uses `f.user.username &&` - the inconsistency is in the web file only.
findings.fix: `const showUsername = Boolean(friend.user.username);` or inline `{friend.user.username && (...)}` to match the other five sites.

findings.issue: `expect(html).not.toContain("@")` asserts a single character is absent from the whole rendered subtree. It passes today only incidentally: any future @-bearing class (Tailwind @container / @md: variants), mailto link, data URI or aria text anywhere inside FriendRequests turns it red for a reason unrelated to the sub-line, and it does not actually assert which element is missing. The rest of this test file is exemplary (imports the real climberHandle, drives the real mounted component, no hardcoded pseudonyms) - this one line is the weak link.
findings.fix:
Assert on the sub-line specifically: query the row's

elements and assert none has textContent starting with '@', or assert container.textContent does not contain `@${username}` for a fixture username.

findings.issue: exactMatchFilter reads clearly and the doc comment explains WHY the username branch has no `mode: "insensitive"` (normalisation at write time). I verified that claim rather than trusting it: the only caller of setUsername is app/app/api/settings/route.ts:225, which passes normalizeUsername(raw).username, and clearUsername only writes null - so every stored username is lowercase and the asymmetry is correct. Two small notes: the inline structural union return type would read better as Prisma.UserWhereInput or a named alias (the union buys nothing since both arms are spread into the same `where`), and `norm.valid && norm.username` is belt-and-braces (valid implies username), fine but worth a word of comment. Test gap: no case covers the reserved/hateful-name reject branch - `q=admin` must return {users:[]} with findFirst never called, which also documents that a legacy row holding a now-reserved username is unreachable by search.
findings.fix: Optional: name the return type, and add 'admin' (reserved) to the existing 'rejects malformed/too-short input before ever touching the DB' loop at app/tests/api/usersSearch.route.test.ts:122.

findings.issue: DuelHome passes placeholder="Search by email or username..." while UserSearch now defaults to the identical string. Two copies of one copy-string that must be updated together - the next tweak will miss one.
findings.fix: Drop the `placeholder` prop at this call site and let the default apply (the prop stays available for other callers).

findings.issue: Scope observation, not a regression (these were 'Player 1'/'-' before and are untouched): the new identity rule stops at the challenge screen. Accepting a challenge navigates straight from 'Swift Ibex 42 challenged you' into a duel room labelled 'Player 1' vs 'Player 2', and the duel leaderboard shows an em dash for the same display_name-null users this change was about. handle.ts describes itself as the single source of truth for 'what do we call this climber', which is not yet true across the duel flow.
findings.fix: Follow-up ticket: route these 8 sites through climberDisplay(playerId, displayName) once the challenge-screen rule is settled. Do not expand this diff.

findings.issue: type="email" -> type="text" inputMode="email" is the right call for a field that now accepts both shapes, and both components already carry autoCapitalize="none" autoCorrect="off", so the mobile-keyboard and first-letter-capitalisation concerns are covered (and normalizeUsername lowercases server-side regardless). Two leftovers worth knowing: the field loses the browser email autofill/validation semantics type=email gave (immaterial here - validation is isSearchable, and autofilling your own email into a friend search is arguably undesirable), and neither search input has a <label> or aria-label (pre-existing, not introduced by this diff; the only context is the 'Add friend' heading above).
findings.fix: Optional in a later a11y pass: add aria-label="Search for a player by email or username" and autoComplete="off" to both inputs.

findings.issue: Positive confirmation of what the dispatch asked me to check, recorded so the next stage need not redo it. (1) Server ids are the right user at all three converted sites: challenge/route.ts uses c.sender_id and createChallenge(uid, ...) makes sender_id === the authenticated uid, with the notification going to recipientId; friends/route.ts looks up `where: { id: uid }` and notifies receiverId (uid is the request sender); friends/[id]/accept looks up `where: { id: uid }` and notifies friendship.sender_id (uid is the accepter). No sender/recipient inversion. (2) The two narrowed selects are clean - `username` has no remaining reader in either route, and climberDisplay(uid, accepter?.display_name) handles a missing row by falling through to the pseudonym. (3) No leftover "Someone"/"Friend"/"User" fallback anywhere in either challenge tree, and no `?? username` chain either. (4) Every changed control has a non-test caller: exactMatchFilter at route.ts:72; the 4 mobile components in mobile/src/screens/ChallengeScreen.tsx:77-89; the 4 web components via DuelHome, rendered by app/duel/page.tsx:16. (5) No debug/console statements added, no scope creep beyond the described files, no schema or dependency change. The only changed thing with NO caller is the vitest @app alias (see the tsconfig warning).

Independently confirming the verifier's process finding: git log shows the implementation landed as 777641d (dated 01:22:02Z) with the software-engineer handoff - which itself claims exitCriteria.committed: false - committed inside the very same commit, and the verifier's tests landed as fa02c30 with its own handoff, which also claims committed: false. Both stages were dispatched as 'leave it uncommitted for review'. No later stage should read 'already committed' as 'already approved'; the critical finding above is exactly what the uncommitted-diff checkpoint exists to catch before history is written.
findings.fix: Orchestrator: the fix for the critical finding needs a follow-up commit (or an amend) on claude/lucid-fermat-3cbvbc; nothing needs reverting. Consider the verifier's proposed `git status --porcelain` vs exitCriteria.committed cross-check at handoff time.

learnings.insight: Relaxing a `displayName && username` sub-line gate to `username &&` only fixes the rows that HAVE a sub-line. The 4 PendingChallenges rows (web + mobile) have no second identity line at all - their secondary slot is the expiry countdown - so the climberDisplay swap there is pure information loss: 'bobsmith challenged you' became 'Swift Ibex 42 challenged you' with the username present in the payload and rendered nowhere. Two facts make it reachable and unrecoverable: ensureUser never writes display_name (so display_name=null is the default for every account), and createChallenge enforces no friendship (so the recipient may have no Friends-List row showing the same person's @handle to cross-reference).
learnings.action: When replacing a name fallback with climberDisplay, enumerate render sites by ROW, not by file, and split them into 'has a secondary identity line' and 'has none'. The second group needs new markup in the same change, or the swap is a regression there. Grep the component for the '@' sub-line before assuming it exists.

learnings.insight: A 'verified by direct code reading' claim in a handoff is not evidence. The verifier skipped render tests for PendingChallenges/FriendsList on the stated ground that they 'apply the identical two-line pattern (climberDisplay + `username &&` sub-line)'; PendingChallenges has no username sub-line in either tree, so the one component with a real behavioural regression is precisely the one that was reasoned about instead of rendered. The same handoff also asserted an idiom ('FriendsListSection uses `username !== null`') that the file contradicts.
learnings.action: When a change applies one rule at N sites, assert the rule at every site or state explicitly which sites are UNCOVERED - never claim the uncovered ones match the pattern. Reviewers: treat every 'verified by code reading' sentence in an upstream handoff as an unverified claim and open the file.

learnings.insight: Adding an @app/* import to a file under app/mobile/src makes that file unreachable from the root TS program, because app/tsconfig.json has no @app/* paths entry (only mobile/tsconfig.json and now vitest.config.mts do) and tsc's `exclude` filters the initial include glob, not the import graph. Verified by compiling the touched component with no paths map: error TS2307: Cannot find module '@app/lib/handle' (and there is no @app package in node_modules to save it). Practical effect: the moment a mobile component imports @app/*, no vitest .tsx test can import it - even relatively - without breaking `pnpm typecheck`, so the mobile tree silently becomes both typecheck-unguarded (root tsconfig excludes mobile) and test-unguarded.
learnings.action: Adding the first @app/* import to a mobile file is a 3-way config change: mobile/vite.config.mts + app/vitest.config.mts + app/tsconfig.json paths. Add "@app/*": ["./src/*"] (no baseUrl needed) in the same commit, and land one test through the alias - an alias with zero importers is config nobody has proven.

learnings.insight: Sweeping for a placeholder by its string ('Someone') misses siblings of the same class: grepping `?? username` app-wide surfaced two challenge notification sites still reading display_name ?? username ?? 'Your opponent' (challenge accept + decline), so one challenge flow now names the same person 'Swift Ibex 42' in one push and 'bobsmith' in the next. The implementer had already widened scope to 'Friend'/'User' on the consistency argument and still missed these, because the search key was the literal placeholder rather than the fallback chain.
learnings.action: Sweep by the PATTERN being replaced (`?? username`, `display_name ??`), not by the placeholder literal, and grep the whole app rather than the two component directories named in the brief. Enumerate every notification type in a flow (received/accepted/declined/expired) before declaring the flow converted.

learnings.insight: Review scope: 2 commits, 17 files, +251/-61 production lines plus 334 test lines. 16 identity render sites audited (12 correct, 4 critical), 5 server notification sites audited (3 converted and id-correct, 2 missed). Spot-check only, per dispatch: the 2 new test files run 10/10 pass in 815ms (the verifier's 748-test baseline was not re-run). One decisive experiment: tsc on a touched mobile component without a paths map -> TS2307, confirming the tsconfig gap is real rather than theoretical.
learnings.action: qa-acceptance: after the fix lands, exercise the Incoming/Sent challenge rows on BOTH /duel (web) and the native Challenge screen with a user whose display_name is null and username is set, and with a challenge from a NON-friend - that is the state the automated tests still do not cover.
